summary.en: Use the **past simple** for finished actions at a finished time: _yesterday_, _in 2019_, _last summer_, _when I was a child_. Use the **present perfect** when no time is given, when the period is still going on (_today_, _this week_, _so far_), or when a past action matters now. A quick test: if you could answer the question "When exactly?", you probably need the past simple.
summary.es: En español peninsular decimos «he comido» para hoy y «comí» para ayer, y la regla inglesa se parece, pero es más estricta: con cualquier momento terminado y concreto (yesterday, last year, in 2019, ago) solo vale el past simple.

form: Past simple: subject + past form (**worked**, **went**); questions and negatives with **did**

uses.text: **Finished time** → past simple: _I **saw** her last Tuesday._
**Unfinished time or no time** → present perfect: _I've **seen** her twice this week._
**News with a result now** → present perfect first, then past simple for the details: _The council **has closed** the bridge. It **made** the decision this morning._

note.en: News reports often open in the present perfect and continue in the past simple.
note.es: Las noticias suelen abrir con present perfect y seguir en past simple.

uses.text: **Life experience** → present perfect: _Have you ever **tried** surfing?_ As soon as you say when, switch: _Yes, I **tried** it in Portugal two years ago._

**Duration up to now** → present perfect with _for_ or _since_: _We've **lived** here since 2020._ For a finished period, use the past simple: _We **lived** in Leeds for five years_ (we don't live there now).

mistakes.wrong: I have finished the report yesterday.

why.en: Yesterday is a finished time, so the present perfect is not possible.
why.es: Con un momento terminado (yesterday, ago, last week) no se usa el present perfect, aunque en español digamos «he terminado».

why.en: A situation that started in the past and continues now takes the present perfect, not the present simple.
why.es: «Vivo aquí desde 2020» se dice con present perfect.

why.en: Questions with when ask about a specific time, so they take the past simple.
why.es: When pregunta por un momento concreto: past simple.

examples.en: I've lost my keys, so I can't get into the flat.
examples.es: He perdido las llaves, así que no puedo entrar en el piso.

examples.en: I lost my keys on the bus last night.
examples.es: Perdí las llaves en el autobús anoche.

examples.en: Have you ever been to Scotland?
We went to Edinburgh for a weekend in March.
She has worked for the council since 2018.
He worked in a bank for ten years before he retrained as a nurse.
The train has just left, and the next one isn't for twenty minutes.
I haven't had any coffee today.
Did you watch the match on Saturday?
Prices have risen sharply this year.

practice.prompt: I ___ my homework an hour ago.

explanation.en: An hour ago is a finished time, so only the past simple works.
The result is visible now and no time is given: present perfect.

practice.prompt: How long ___ in this flat? Since last spring.

explanation.en: Since last spring shows the situation continues now: present perfect.
